newsitem.title: UK: NWE cracked fuel oil markets stable in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: NWE cracked fuel oil markets stable in dull trade.

text.p: NWE cracked fuel oil markets were stable on Tuesday, but trade was dull with opposing factors putting the spot market in the doldrums looking for fresh direction, traders said.

Firmer crude and high sulphur cargo pricing gave the market some upside impetus, but this was capped by a weaker nearby paper market and relaxed buying interest, leaving outright prices little changed on the day.

High sulphur fuel oil barges edged higher in early business with several traders seen pricing cargoes to take transatlantic as part of a regular exchange for sugar deal with Cuba. However, there was little sign of the aggressive buying from one trade house that pushed values higher on Monday.
Against the pricing high sulphur barges were traded at a steady $89 fob ARA in early business but trade into the bunker market was concluded later at $87 a tonne fob ARA.
High sulphur cargoes were offered at a steady $87 cif NWE but good supplies saw relaxed buyers around $2-3 under this level.
Low sulphur barge prices held steady. Traders said tight prompt supply was balanced by slack demand and the market talked in a wide range between $93 and $96 a tonne fob ARA.
A plentiful supply kept low sulphur cargo prices pegged back. Fob stems valued around $93 a tonne.
